key_insight: GLM-5 introduces an efficiency-first design that shifts 'vibe coding' toward 'agentic engineering' by using DSA to cut training/inference costs while preserving long-context reasoning and by using an asynchronous RL pipeline to speed post-training alignment.
problem_solved: High computational cost and slow post-training alignment of large foundation models, while retaining long-context fidelity and agentic capabilities for reasoning and coding.
method: Apply DSA (an efficiency-focused training/inference technique) to drastically reduce compute and memory overhead while maintaining long-context fidelity.
Introduce an asynchronous reinforcement learning infrastructure that decouples alignment/autonomy updates from base model training to improve post-training efficiency.
Build on prior ARC (agentic, reasoning, coding) capabilities to transition model behavior from style-driven 'vibe coding' to controlled, agentic engineering.
impact: Practitioners gain a path to deploy more capable, long-context foundation models with much lower compute cost and faster alignment cycles, enabling practical agentic applications and cheaper iteration for research and products.

paper_title: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
